title: How to Decide, Convey vs. Convince, & More

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast. Today we have another one of our early book launch episodes for a new book coming out next week by expert decision strategist and leading world series of poker player Annie Duke.. You can catch the podcast we did with her a couple years ago for the paperback release of her first book, Thinking in Betts.

key_points.evidence_quote: But in this episode, we talk about her new book, how to decide, which picks up where the last book left off, and the discussion that follows covers lots of useful strategies, tools, and mindsets for helping all kinds of people and organizations decide under conditions of uncertainty.

key_points.text: Annie is interviewed by A6 and Z managing partner Jeff Jordan, who was previously CEO and then executive chairman of Open Table.
key_points.evidence_quote: Annie is interviewed by A6 and Z managing partner Jeff Jordan, who was previously CEO and then executive chairman of Open Table, former GM of eBay North America, and much more.

thesis: Annie Duke argues that learning from experience is often frustrated by the paradox of experience, where individuals derive bad lessons from single data points due to result bias and hindsight bias. She proposes using tools like reconstructing the state of knowledge at the time of a decision and analyzing outcomes through a four-quadrant matrix of decision quality versus outcome quality to improve decision-making processes under uncertainty.
